obligations.scenario: The three streams are each read bit by bit starting at bs_*[0], with the first bit read serving as the most significant bit of the codeword. Match the first complete code using the fixed code table below. The upper 4 bits of symbol are run, and the lower 4 bits are category. 0x00 is EOB; 0xf0 represents 16 zeros. For category>0, continue reading category bits to form an 8-bit shift buffer v (retaining the last 8 bits when more than 8 bits are read), with mask being the low 8 bits of (2^category-1); for category1..8, take v&mask if bit category-1 of v is 1; otherwise take the low 8 bits of (v&mask)-mask and interpret them as signed. category9/10 follows the else branch because the index is outside 8 bits. Random stimulus is not classified as illegal solely because the text omits a length-budget/retry assertion: the concrete generation must demonstrate a length>1024 or capacity>64 path. A possible combinatorial maximum is insufficient evidence of an actually generated out-of-domain transaction. Missing an explicit bound on random lengths may reduce setup by one grade, while independent directed legal boundary cases remain full credit.
obligations.checked_target: The code table defines the symbol facts; input lengths may end at code boundaries, and unfilled coefficients are 0.

obligations.scenario: The acceptance edge is age0. For each channel, h is 2 times the total number of Huffman code bits read, plus category+2 for each record with category>0, plus 1 for EOB; add another 2 if the length is exhausted without EOB. r is the sum of run+1 for each nonzero-termination record before RLE stops, plus 2; if no record with run=0 and 8-bit amplitude=0 occurs, likewise add 2 when the records are exhausted. Let i=h+r+2; completion is then at age=max(iY+225,iCb+160,iCr+160)+66, the Y bit count is updated at age=hY+1, and the trigger match is updated at age=iY+1.
obligations.checked_target: This timing is guaranteed only for legal, complete bitstreams within the transaction domain; asynchronous reset need not wait for completion.

O1.definition: Reset for three cycles before starting; reset again before the 8th transaction to clear the sticky trigger; also interrupt decoding with reset after approximately 20 cycles, then resend. Drive on falling edges, and observe outputs 1ns after assertion. Other legal histories covering the same behavior are allowed; reference numbering/counts are not mandatory.

O2.definition: The three channels use independent encoders to generate legal records, including EOB, positive and negative categories, short and long codes, category1..10 (including native truncation of -128, 256, -511, and 1023), different channel lengths, exhaustion exactly at a record boundary without EOB, and a category10 record truncated to zero followed by nonzero records; 16 serialized tasks, with random coefficients in the range -127..127. Other legal histories covering the same behavior are allowed; reference numbering/counts are not mandatory.

O3.definition: Empty blocks, nonzero DC, EOB after 63 nonzero coefficients, and sparse coefficients (naturally producing ZRL), encoded across all 64 positions, with an independent model reconstructing the entire block. Other legal histories covering the same behavior are allowed; reference numbering/counts are not mandatory.

O4.definition: The 3rd transaction matches the Y diagonal with block_num=0, the 4th is identical with block_num=1, and reset clears it at the 8th transaction; nonmatching blocks and nonzero block numbers are interleaved. Other legal histories covering the same behavior are allowed; reference numbering/counts are not mandatory.

O5.definition: Identical blocks before and after triggering, Y values of 127 and negative values, and Cb/Cr remaining independent channels; random sparse blocks. Other legal histories covering the same behavior are allowed; reference numbering/counts are not mandatory.

O6.definition: DC, sparse nonzero coefficients, 63 dense positions, positive and negative coefficients, and all Q indices; random signs and amplitudes with different seeds. Other legal histories covering the same behavior are allowed; reference numbering/counts are not mandatory.

O7.definition: Nonzero columns/rows, DC, sparse and dense blocks; including diagonal trigger vectors and random positions, with positive and negative intermediate values. Other legal histories covering the same behavior are allowed; reference numbering/counts are not mandatory.

O8.definition: Independent random signs and values for Y/Cb/Cr, positive and negative chroma, centered empty blocks, and larger coefficients triggering RGB clamping. Other legal histories covering the same behavior are allowed; reference numbering/counts are not mandatory.

O9.definition: Different bitstream lengths, especially short Y with dense Cb, as well as dense Y; compare the completion pulse, consumed bit count, and final RGB. Other legal histories covering the same behavior are allowed; reference numbering/counts are not mandatory.

O10.definition: After driving each transaction, continue up to the 4000-cycle limit; the sequence independently derives expected timing by parsing according to the model and checks done at the same time; on timeout, record UVM_ERROR and continue normally. Other legal histories covering the same behavior are allowed; reference numbering/counts are not mandatory.
